details: The latest US inflation data for September revealed an unexpected rise in both consumer and wholesale prices, primarily driven by increased energy costs. This hotter-than-anticipated inflation has intensified expectations for the Federal Reserve to maintain tight monetary policy and potentially implement further interest rate hikes. The news led to a sharp decline in the cryptocurrency market, with Bitcoin falling below $81,000 and significant liquidations in futures contracts.
title: US Inflation Surges, Triggering Crypto Market Decline

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its October Global Financial Stability Report, highlighted three increasing risks to global financial stability: a potential correction in AI-related markets, a sharp rise in sovereign bond yields, and cyberattacks. The IMF cautioned that these factors could lead to an abrupt tightening of financial conditions, increasing market turmoil and negatively impacting various asset classes, including cryptocurrencies.
title: IMF Warns of Financial Risks from AI Correction, Rising Bond Yields

details: New research from the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) indicates that increases in US bank deposit interest rates are associated with a significant slowdown in stablecoin market capitalization growth. The study found that a one-basis-point rise in deposit rates correlated with approximately three percentage points less stablecoin growth over a ten-week period, suggesting that rising traditional finance returns may be drawing capital away from stablecoins.
title: BIS Research: Rising Bank Deposit Rates Slow Stablecoin Growth
